Manual CPU/GPU ranges can override software frequency caps. Hardware, firmware and other thermal protections are not changed. Increased heat and power use are possible.

Allow manual CPU/GPU ranges to bypass software frequency caps? This can cause overheating, instability, faster battery wear or permanent damage. It does not add overclock frequencies or disable hardware protection, and other firmware or thermal limits may still apply. Bypass only affects manually selected ranges and resets at reboot. Enable only if you understand and accept these risks.

Choose an interval from the frequencies supported by this GPU. Software cooling caps remain active unless you explicitly enable bypass on the CPU page. A high minimum increases heat and battery use. The GPU can still power down when idle.

Board (quiet_therm)

Readings come from the Android thermal service and readable kernel sensors. CPU and GPU values prefer explicitly identified hardware zones. Without a surface reading from the HAL, the board card shows quiet_therm, not a calibrated casing temperature. Missing measurements remain unavailable. Android thermal status is unavailable without HAL readings; it is not an independent safety check and may not reflect manual bypass.
